passage: It started with a burnt dosa. My mother said, "You never watch the stove," and something in me snapped. I told her I was sick of the comments on my flat, my job, my friends, and the way she told Himani, my wife, what to buy. Then I said she had ruined our first year of marriage. My father stood up. Words came out that I cannot take back. The thing I had meant to ask, that they call before visiting, never got said. By evening nobody was speaking, and the only thing anyone remembered was the last sentence I shouted. I have thought about it many times: I had a fair request, and I buried it under years of complaints. - Vikram

qa.q: What did the quarrel start with?
qa.a: It started with a burnt dosa.

qa.q: What was Vikram feeling underneath the outburst?
qa.a: Vikram was feeling built-up frustration from years of comments, which came out all at once.
Vikram could apologise for the shouting and later ask calmly, on its own, for the parents to call before visiting.

qa.q: How might Vikram's mother have felt when the request got lost?
qa.a: Vikram's mother may have felt hurt and confused, since the only thing that came through was the anger.

grounding: After a small quarrel Vikram blurts out a long-held complaint about the parents' interference, and the real request gets lost.
